title: Bible R.E.C.A.P.
markdown:
The Bible R.E.C.A.P. is available in the Bible on this site. [Read the NET Bible >>>](/bible/John/1)

> All Scripture is inspired by God and is useful to teach us what is true and to make us realize what is wrong in our lives. It corrects us when we are wrong and teaches us to do what is right. God uses it to prepare and equip his people to do every good work. (2 Timothy 3:16–17, NLT)

When you renew your mind with the truth of God’s Word and follow what it says, you become more like Christ. The Word of God is the language of the Holy Spirit. He will open your mind to understand it and give you power to obey it. Whenever you read, ask the Holy Spirit to guide you into all truth (John 16:13). Then trust His guidance and ask one or more of these five questions.

## Five Questions to Ask

![R — Is there a REVELATION about God that I should embrace? Revelation is who God is. Highlight: orange. E — Is there an EXAMPLE I should follow or avoid? Highlight: light blue. C — Is there a COMMAND I should obey? Highlight: red. A — Is there something I need to APPLY to my life? Application is what this passage asks of you that is not already a command, an example, or a promise. Highlight: green. P — Is there a PROMISE I should claim? Highlight: purple.](/bible-resources/images/recap-five-questions.png)

You do not have to force all five. One clear answer is enough. Some verses do not have fit any of them.

## An Example

John 3:16 reveals God’s love in giving His Son, so you can highlight the verse with orange (Revelation). John 13:15 is an example to follow; Judas in the same chapter is an example to avoid, so you can highlight those verses with light blue (Example). John 13:34 is a command to love one another, so you can highlight the verse with red (Command). John 15:5 asks you to abide, because apart from Him you can do nothing, so you can highlight the verse with green (Application). John 14:21 is a promise that Jesus will manifest Himself to those who love and obey Him, so you can highlight the verse with purple (Promise).

Identifying by the letter is what matters. Using color is optional. Mark the passage with a letter—R, E, C, A, or P— so you can find it again in your notes.

## Treasure Them in Your Heart

Write down what you have discovered from the reading and your reflection. Thank Him for His revelations, examples, commands, applications, and promises that are to mature your new identity in Christ and make you fruitful in the good works He prepared for you. Treasure them in your heart and put them into practice.
